title: PR Code Review Output
description: Standard schema for code review results produced by agent reviewers

version.description: Schema payload version for PR review artifacts

base_branch.description: Target branch for merge (e.g., main, FBS_Integration)

base_sha.description: Merge-base commit SHA (where feature branch diverged from base)

head_sha.description: Feature branch HEAD commit SHA at time of review

bubbles.description: List of Issue ID that are *currently bubbled* for developer review

reviewers.description: List of reviewer names or agent IDs

verdict.description: Final verdict: must be explicit about merge readiness and any blockers

strengths.description: Bullet-point list of positive findings, design choices, test coverage

bubble_up.description: Issues raised by reviewers that exit Phase 5 unresolved. Includes all issues *ever bubbled.* Mirrors items[] in the pr-team skill's bubble_ups.schema.json sidecar. pr-review and pr-team workflows write this array directly into the consolidated review JSON; the schema enforces the shape, not the policy. Empty array is valid (no bubbled items). See `classification.description` below for per-value semantics.
bubble_up.$comment: Inline mirror (not $ref) because this schema is draft-07 and the sibling is draft-2020-12; cross-dialect $ref is fragile.

classification.description: Why this issue is bubbled. architectural_ambiguity = two or more reasonable weight-bearing resolutions exist (user decision required); out_of_scope = real issue but outside this PR's scope; needs_follow_up = net-new work exceeding Phase 5 mechanical scope; fixer_failed = a Phase 5 fixer attempted the issue and returned FAIL.

reason.description: One-line freetext explanation. For 'fixer_failed', includes the fixer's FAIL REASON (e.g., 'fixer FAIL: missing file at path X'). Capped at 200 chars to mirror the FAIL REASON contract in pr-team return_contract.md.

post_review_resolutions.description: Resolutions applied immediately after review, before the action plan begins. Tracks items resolved in the review session itself (rule updates, quick fixes, reclassifications).

verification_log.description: One of three shapes: (1) 'skipped' advisory for catalog-style review JSONs; (2) the canonical nested two-block structure populated by pr-review Phase 1/3 (dispatch_time) and Phase 4 (pre_fix_time) - used by all new JSONs; (3) a legacy flat shape kept for backward compatibility with pre-2026-05 review JSONs. New review JSONs MUST use (1) or (2). Drift between this contract and the pr-review SKILL.md is caught by the harness test tests/schemas/test_pr_review_schema_verification_log.py.

oneOf.description: Canonical nested two-block shape. dispatch_time is populated during Phase 1 / Phase 3 atomic close; pre_fix_time is populated during Phase 4. Each inner sub-object MUST contain raw command output - stdout fields are paste captures, not summaries. The literal string 'OK', a paraphrase, or a one-line summary in any stdout field is a STUB and fails the corresponding done-criterion.

pr_metadata_check.description: Phase 1 Check 1 - gh pr view authoritative metadata fetch. All three fields required.

command.description: The exact gh pr view command invoked (e.g. `gh pr view <PR> --json number,title,headRefName,baseRefName,state,commits --jq ...`).

stdout.description: Raw paste capture of the command's JSON output. The literal string 'OK' (any case) is rejected by the schema as a STUB; must be the verbatim JSON the gh command emitted.

result.description: Short status: 'OK (state=OPEN)' for a successful check, 'STOP - state=<X>' for a closed/merged PR.

structural_guards_check.description: Phase 1 Check 2 - structural guard pytest invocation. Mandatory-but-conditional: applies=false when the path filter (Step 1) and content filter (Step 2) both return empty; in that case command and stdout_tail MAY be empty strings. When applies=true, command and stdout_tail MUST contain the full invocation and the verbatim tail of pytest output (including the '=== N passed in Xs ===' summary).

applies.description: True if Phase 1 Check 2's path filter (Step 1) or content filter (Step 2) matched any PR file. False if both filters returned empty (the gate is mandatory-but-conditional and was correctly skipped).

command.description: The full pytest invocation of the project's configured guard suite (`review.guard_suite` in the project's harness config), verbatim as run. Empty string if applies=false.

stdout_tail.description: Last ~10 lines of pytest output verbatim, including the '=== N passed in Xs ===' summary. Empty string if applies=false.

result.description: One of: 'OK (N passed)' if applies=true and all guards green; 'SKIPPED (no CICD/test-infra paths in PR)' if applies=false; 'STOP - guards red' if any guard failed (this halts dispatch).

pre_fix_time.description: Phase 4 branch-safety log. At Phase 3 write time this is the literal pending string; Phase 4 first-run replaces it in-place with the full five-check struct. The pending string is the ONLY acceptable placeholder - any other text is a stub and fails the Phase 4 hand-off check.

oneOf.const: pending - to be populated in Phase 4

current_branch_check.description: Phase 4 Check 1 - current branch read via git rev-parse. stdout is the raw branch name; the literal string 'OK' is invalid here because `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` never emits 'OK'.

command.description: The exact git command, e.g. `git -C $REPO rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`.

stdout.description: Raw stdout verbatim - e.g. '115-DEV-get_schema_03'. The literal string 'OK' (any case) is rejected by the schema because `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` never emits 'OK'; must be the actual branch name.

result.description: Short status: 'OK' if the branch was read successfully.

branch_match_check.description: Phase 4 Check 2 - assert current branch equals headRefName from Phase 1 Check 1. Pure equality assertion; carries the two compared values for audit.

assertion.description: Literal assertion string for the equality check.

current_branch.description: The branch name from current_branch_check.stdout - verbatim.

head_ref_name.description: The headRefName value from Phase 1 Check 1's pr_metadata_check.stdout - verbatim.

result.description: Outcome: 'OK (match)' on success, 'STOP - mismatch' on failure.

clean_tree_check.description: Phase 4 Check 3 - `git status --porcelain` clean-tree assertion. stdout MAY be the empty string (which IS the affirmative 'clean' claim); a stdout of the literal 'OK' is a LIE because `git status --porcelain` never emits 'OK'. result describes inspection outcome (clean OR dirty with per-file disposition).

command.description: The exact git command, e.g. `git -C $REPO status --porcelain`.

stdout.description: Raw `git status --porcelain` output verbatim, pre-exclusion. For clean-tree assertion semantics, see filtered_stdout (post-exclusion stdout - empty IS the affirmative clean claim).

filtered_stdout.description: Post-exclusion stdout - the output of `git status --porcelain` filtered through git_status_filter_excluded.py. Empty string IS the affirmative clean-tree claim.

exclusions_fixture.description: Repo-relative path to the machine-generated exclusions JSON used for this check (e.g. `reference/git_curated/machine_generated_exclusions.json`). Records which exclusions list governed the branch-safety check.

result.description: Inspection outcome: 'OK (empty)' for a clean tree, or 'DIRTY - inspected: [<file1>: unrelated, stashed | file2: committed]' with per-file disposition.

sha_ancestry_check.description: Phase 4 Check 4 - verify both base_sha and head_sha are ancestors of HEAD via two `git merge-base --is-ancestor` invocations. Exit codes are integers (0 = ancestor, 1 = not ancestor).

base_sha.description: From Phase 1 Check 1 first_sha - the merge-base SHA being verified.

head_sha.description: From Phase 1 Check 1 last_sha - the HEAD SHA being verified.

base_ancestor_command.description: The exact git invocation, e.g. `git merge-base --is-ancestor <base_sha> HEAD`.

base_ancestor_exit.description: Exit code from the base-ancestor command. 0 means base_sha is an ancestor of HEAD; 1 means it is not (which halts review).

head_ancestor_command.description: The exact git invocation, e.g. `git merge-base --is-ancestor <head_sha> HEAD`.

head_ancestor_exit.description: Exit code from the head-ancestor command. 0 means head_sha is an ancestor of HEAD; 1 means it is not (which halts review).

result.description: Combined outcome: 'OK (both ancestors)' on success, 'STOP - <which> not ancestor' on failure.

base_branch_recorded.description: Phase 4 Check 5 - capture the verbatim baseRefName from gh. value is NOT always 'main'; many repos default to 'dev' or another integration branch. source documents the gh command that produced value.

source.description: The gh command that produced value, e.g. `gh pr view <PR> --json baseRefName --jq .baseRefName`.

value.description: Verbatim baseRefName from the gh command - NOT always 'main'. Many repos default to 'dev' or another integration branch.

oneOf.description: Legacy flat shape - pre-contract JSONs. Do NOT use for new review JSONs.

id.description: Issue ID from the review (e.g., C1, I9, M4)

status.description: RESOLVED = fixed in session; DOWNGRADED = severity reduced with rationale; CLOSED_NO_ACTION = not applicable or excluded

evidence.description: What was done: commit SHA, file changed, rule updated, or rationale for downgrade/exclusion

id.description: Issue ID (C=critical, I=important, M=minor, followed by number)

step.description: Optional: workflow step name (for CI/CD issues)

both_reviewers.description: True if multiple reviewers identified this issue independently

reviewer.description: Optional: specific reviewer if not both

summary.description: Detailed explanation of the issue, including impact and evidence

fix.description: One-or-more actionable remediation options (code snippet, command, or approach)

fix_kind.description: Optional: mechanical = the fix follows from the text alone (a haiku fixer suffices); judgment = the fix needs design judgment. Recorded per finding by each reviewer; merge keeps judgment when merged findings disagree; absent reads as judgment. Fix-wave planning picks the fixer model from it.
